title: Can heavy metals cause brain fog / depersonalization?

grade.title: No qualifying human study in this corpus
grade.basis: No qualifying human study was located.

answerHtml: No study in this corpus tested brain fog or depersonalization as an outcome of metal exposure or of a detox protocol. Neurodevelopmental endpoints for lead and methylmercury are different outcomes and are described on those metal pages. They are not a finding about brain fog.

sections.heading: Nearby evidence that is a different question
sections.html: The TLC trial found no cognitive benefit from succimer in children with blood lead of 20 to 44 µg/dL. That is a null cognitive result at those levels, not a study of brain fog in adults. Rogan 2001.

heavyMetalIndexHtml: Heavy Metal Index health pages. This Heavy Metal Index URL returned HTTP 200 on 15 October 2026. Figures on this page are not copied from that index. They come from the sources named above.
buyHtml:
The Heavy Metal Tested and Certified public register listed no licensees on 15 October 2026. That page reported 0 certified brands and 0 certified products, and it stated that no brand has completed the three-lot baseline. A specimen layout on the register is an illustration, not a licensee. This page does not name or rank any brand.

The program states that certification is a measurement of a product against a published limit, not a statement that the product is safe. If a licensee is later listed for this category, it will be on the register.
